findings.reason: The original standalone tile contains only the definition. An age–time picture materially clarifies which boundary supplies each characteristic and why newborn cohorts cannot meet the absorbing cutoff during the shorter horizon. This is a warranted explanatory-diagram addition under the expanded scope, rather than a claim that the original prose is mathematically incomplete.
findings.action: Added a fenced TikZ illustration and explanatory Remarks preserving the complete Definition.

correction: Added an age–time diagram showing initial density, renewal inflow, the a=t branch separator, a speed-one initial cohort ending at A, and a newborn cohort ending at T below A.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Age–time strip 0<=t<=T, 0<=a<=A with 0<T<A; t horizontal and a vertical.
diagram_math_checks.check: The schematic uses T at x=4 and A at y=6, so the diagonal a=t meets t=T below a=A. The left boundary is the prescribed initial density n_0^A; the lower boundary is renewal inflow B_A(t); the upper boundary is absorbing outflow.

Both coordinate increments are 2, hence da/dt=1 and a-t=4 remains constant. It lies in a>=t and terminates at a=A; no continuation above the cutoff is drawn. The endpoint marks arrival/removal, not an extra boundary value for the open-domain density.
diagram_math_checks.basis: Assigned Definition: speed 1, initial branch a>=t, cohort removed on reaching A.

diagram_math_checks.check: da/dt=1, a=t-t_b, and 0<t_b<T. It stays in a<t and has final age T-t_b<T<A. Its arrow points toward increasing time and age; it never meets absorbing outflow. The caption gives the general bound for t_b<=t<=T.
diagram_math_checks.basis: Assigned Definition: newborn branch a<t and no newborn cohort reaches A because A>T; supplier characteristic formula and a'(s)=1.

diagram_math_checks.check: Cohort paths are kinematic; the survival factor S changes density rather than characteristic speed. No curve thickness encodes density, fertility or survival. The original definition and characteristic formula remain unchanged and independent of the diagram.
